full_text_en:
Application of Pozzolo Shipping Supplies Company of Italy for Arrest of the Vessel "Gulf Grain"

Applicant: Pozzolo Shipping Supplies Company of Italy.

Respondent: Gulf East Ship Management Co., Ltd. (Hong Kong).

On March 9, 1991, the Applicant, Pozzolo Shipping Supplies Company of Italy, filed an application with the Dalian Maritime Court of the People's Republic of China for pre-litigation arrest of a vessel. The application stated that: Between August 24 and September 28, 1990, at ports including Chioggia, Marghera, and Navarra in Italy, the Applicant repeatedly supplied food, deck stores, engine stores, and other materials to the vessel "Gulf Grain," owned by the Respondent, Gulf East Ship Management Co., Ltd. (Hong Kong), with the total value being 2,955,112 Italian lire. The above facts are confirmed by documents duly signed and sealed by the master of the vessel. Although the Applicant repeatedly urged payment, the Respondent failed to pay. The vessel "Gulf Grain" is currently berthed at Dalian Port. The Applicant requests the arrest of the vessel and an order that the Respondent provide cash security in the amount of USD 40,000 or other reliable and satisfactory security in another form. The Applicant is willing to bear all legal liabilities arising from any wrongful arrest.

Upon receiving the application, the Dalian Maritime Court, after review, found that the Applicant's application complied with Article 1, Paragraph 8 of the Specific Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Pre-litigation Arrest of Vessels. With the approval of the President, the Court ruled on March 11, 1991 as follows: 1. Effective from this date, the Respondent's vessel "Gulf Grain" is to be arrested. 2. The Respondent is ordered to provide, within 30 days from this date, cash security of USD 40,000 or other reliable security in another form.

After the issuance of the ruling and the arrest order signed by the President, the Respondent did not provide any form of security. Before the expiration of the 30-day arrest period, the Applicant, naming the Respondent as defendant, filed a lawsuit with the Dalian Maritime Court on April 8, 1991, regarding a dispute over the cost of the ship supply contract. The Dalian Maritime Court, upon review, found that the case met the requirements of Article 6, Paragraph 3 of the Specific Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Pre-litigation Arrest of Vessels. On April 9, the Court decided to docket the case and on April 11 issued a notice of response to the defendant.

After receiving the notice of response, the defendant negotiated with the plaintiff and the parties reached a settlement agreement, whereby the defendant paid off all outstanding amounts. Subsequently, on April 12, the plaintiff, on the ground that its claim had been satisfied, filed an application for withdrawal of the lawsuit with the Dalian Maritime Court.

After reviewing the plaintiff's withdrawal application, the Dalian Maritime Court found that the lawful rights and obligations of both parties had been realized. Pursuant to Article 131, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Court ruled on April 12 to grant the plaintiff's withdrawal of the lawsuit. At the same time, the President issued an order to lift the arrest of the vessel "Gulf Grain."
